content.text:
## Summary

I reviewed the **#core-infra** channel history and identified the full thread discussing the OOM / memory-pressure incident on the inference cluster (starting with the alert "High memory pressure on cluster-b inference pods. OOM kills detected." and running through the root-cause investigation and revert).

**Three people actively posted in that incident thread:**

| Name | Slack Username | Role in discussion |
|---|---|---|
| **Priya Sharma** | priya.sharma | Posted the initial OOM alert, pulled memory profiles/pprof deltas, diagnosed the CUDA allocation limit, and executed the batch-size revert |
| **Łukasz Kowalski** | lukas.kowalski | Pushed back on treating the revert as a full fix, suggested checking for memory leaks/tensor allocation issues, guided the `pprof --base` diff analysis |
| **Olena Petrenko** | olena.petrenko | Flagged her evicted training job as a symptom, checked `model_cache_hit_rate`, ran a local repro, and profiled per-batch memory footprint post-revert |

Note: A fourth user, **Robert** (U_ROBERT), also appears later in the same channel, but only in a **separate, unrelated conversation** about the monthly cloud cost overrun — not in the OOM/memory-pressure incident thread — so I excluded him from this list.

<done>
Identified the three Slack users who discussed the OOM/memory-pressure incident on the inference cluster in #core-infra: **Priya Sharma (priya.sharma)**, **Łukasz Kowalski (lukas.kowalski)**, and **Olena Petrenko (olena.petrenko)**. These are the names to list as reviewers on the incident postmortem doc. (A separate later conversation involving Robert was confirmed to be an unrelated cloud-cost discussion, not part of this incident.)
</done>
